- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent prices are trending up.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and continues upward; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; forecast should adjust upward 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion is common in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 3–5 days (e.g., >10% error), apply “early correction” rule: adjust forecast downward if sentiment is weak, upward if sentiment is strong.
- Sentiment history with alternating 0.33/1.00 patterns suggests model is overfitting to short-term sentiment; use smoothing or lagged sentiment weights for 3–5 day horizon.
